newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel gets Strauss-Kahn assurances on EMU drive.
newsitem.headline: Waigel gets Strauss-Kahn assurances on EMU drive.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Monday said he had spoken with his French counterpart Dominique Strauss-Kahn by telephone, who assured he would do everything to meet the targets for European monetary union.

Waigel said any move by France to raise taxes should not be seen as "creative accounting" but real measures aimed at meeting the Maastricht targets. However, they should be followed by structural reform.

"The French are aware of their responsibilities," Waigel told reporters on the way to a meeting of his Christian Social Union (CSU), adding that France would not stop at limiting its budget deficit to 3.5 to 3.6 percent of economic output.
He said he had spoken recently to Strauss-Kahn on the telephone and that the French finance minister told him "he wanted to do everything from tax measures to budget measures to meet three percent".

The Maastricht treaty on economic and monetary union (EMU) expects participants to restrict their budget deficits to three percent of gross domestic product in 1997 to qualify for the 1999 launch of Europe's single currency.
While rejecting that any tax hike in France to meet the Maastricht targets could be seen as creative accounting, Waigel said that all countries, Germany included, must enact structural reforms.
"We are all faced with this," he said.
Nevertheless, Waigel added he did not consider it "proper form as a German to give lessons to the finance minister of France".
